name: Billie Eilish
notes: Whisper-register alt-pop built by subtraction. The research's drum claim is a negative one — "minimalist to the point of subtraction: a single kick, amplified finger snaps, and foley in place of a hat pattern; where hats appear they are 16ths or trap 32nd rolls used as a fill, not a bed" — so `hihat.continuous` is false, `fillDensity` collapses to 0.12, the roll vocabulary keeps 32nds but at a very low `freqPerBar`, and the perc lanes are snap-led. "Velocity range is deliberately narrow and quiet" is the `velocityTiers` block, which is the one place a mix instruction becomes a number. The backbeat is "usually implied rather than struck — where a kit exists it is 2&4 straight", so `halfTime` is false and the snare is `backbeat_24` with a very low ghost probability. Keys and mode come straight from the entry: "E minor, F♯ minor, D♭ minor, G minor recur" and "bad guy is G minor with a i—iv—V7 frame", encoded as ["i","iv","V"] with the seventh in `extensions` because a numeral names a degree and never a quality. "Her writing tolerates a tonic-only drone for whole sections" is the single-chord family and the `vamp` weighting. The 808 is authored because the entry names it outright — "synth bass, a kick drum … and 808 bass" — as `counter_riff` rather than `bassline`, so the distorted sub sits as a texture under the sung line while the synth bass keeps generating; that is the lane's own boundary rule ("this lane keeps names whose 808 use is a texture under a sung melody"). Melody register is the documented "bad guy" span F3—C6 written low, with "narrow and speech-like, mostly stepwise inside a 5th" as the interval spread and `motifPitchCount`. The arrangement is the entry's own list — "near-silent intro; verse and chorus often use the same harmonic loop with the chorus distinguished by bass entry alone" — so no `prechorus` length is declared: the research names no pre-chorus for her and neither structure uses one. ⚠ The INFERRED parameters are the velocity tiers, every drum probability, the humanize pair and `bpm.mode` 107 (the research gives 60—135 with a working cluster at 90—125, so the mode is that cluster's midpoint). ⚠ The catalogue-wide tempo reading carries the research's [LOW-CONF] mark. ⚠ **The bass is `mirror_kick` rather than the held `reese_sustain` the research describes** — *“the sub is the arrangement's whole low end — ”synth bass, a kick drum … and 808 bass” — often distorted and pushed so far forward that it functions as the lead. Slides are used sparingly; the bass rarely doubles the vocal.”* — and that is a limit of the engine rather than a reading of the record. `generators::phrase_spans` re-articulates a held span only when it runs longer than two bars, so over the four-bar clip `reese_sustain` writes at most four notes and cannot reach the 500-bassline floor `engine/tests/bass.rs` holds every model to. `mobb-deep`, `dmx` and `capone-n-noreaga` carry the same substitution for the same reason; `followRootsProb` stays where it was so the line still reads as roots under the chord. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 974/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980 (2026-08-17, counter variety floor).** The 1-bar value came out of `melody.phraseBars`, which is now [2,4] weighted [4,1]. `generators::melody` writes a phrase's rhythm **once** and reuses it for every repeat, so a 1-bar phrase gives the whole clip one bar of rhythmic entropy — and the counter, whose onsets are read off the lead's, inherits that ceiling. Distinctness is combinatorial in the shape LENGTH, not in the option count. ⚠ The value that moved here is INFERRED rather than a researched claim — the entry's Melody/chords line reads "ukulele/piano/guitar sketch harmonised with close, stacked, close-mic'd harmonies ("layers of ethereal harmonies"); melodic contour is narrow and speech-like, mostly stepwise inside a 5th, sitting low in a soprano instrument (documented range across "bad guy": F3–C6). Hooks are rhythmic-syllabic rather than interval-driven.", and every claim in it still holds after the change.
